scope: Public historical static-source retrieval and local safe analysis only; no unknown hosts probed
provenance_policy: Official event records establish event provenance; participant repositories establish file/challenge attribution. Public copy hashes are not organizer authenticity checks.

facts: ETDA/AJCCBC organized Cyber SEA Game 2019 on 20–22 November 2019
Thailand won; ten ASEAN countries participated
Cyber SEA Game 2025 ran in Bangkok on 16–17 October 2025
Vietnam won; Singapore second; Indonesia third
Author reports competing for Singapore online on 26 November 2021
Known Vulnerability 1 begins by reading Server: Apache/2.4.49
Author explicitly says only a remembered subset of challenges is covered; full archive not established
S.1 sections 1.2/3 define a five-unit code; 4.4 defines letter/figure shifts; Table 1 gives code values

cases.evidence: locally reproduced passive reconstruction and image reading
observations: 68 captured frames, 26 FTP control frames and 3 data frames
TShark and independent Scapy packet lengths/payload bytes agree
Stream 2 is 4709-byte FLAG.zip; stream 3 is 49-byte passmemo.txt
Memo password decrypts one 4649-byte FLAG.GIF; visually inspected answer text
cases.helper_observation: inspect returns complete basic classification application/octet-stream; it does not reconstruct streams or extract content
cases.recommendation: Teach FTP control/data linkage, stream reassembly, password-bearing side files and image inspection with Wireshark/tshark and 7-Zip; retain basic helper scope
limitations: Participant-hosted copy, not an organizer checksum
No live connection or platform acceptance tested

cases.evidence: locally reproduced passive field extraction against independent offset parser and author values
observations: 166 frames; TShark NTLMSSP message types 1,2,3 at frames 34,37,39 in TCP stream 0
8-byte server challenge; 326-byte NT response splits into 16-byte proof and 310-byte blob
Raw scan finds a repeated type-2 challenge; do not assume every signature is a distinct exchange
cases.helper_observation: inspect recognizes application/vnd.tcpdump.pcap but does not decode authentication
cases.recommendation: Filter ntlmssp, pair type 2/3 within the same stream, validate NTLMv2 structure before constructing a hashcat line
limitations: No password cracking or relay performed
Packet fields alone do not prove the writeup’s broader poisoning/relay attribution

cases.challenge: C6 A very old odd file
cases.guide_route: Miscellaneous / explicit symbol mapping and stateful text code
cases.evidence: locally reproduced strict failure and explicitly partial decoding baseline
observations: Payload is line 2, containing 2088 dot/dash symbols
417 complete five-bit groups and 3 trailing symbols
Dot=1, dash=0 and normal group order yield Swedish spelling words with 18 shift controls
First letters and explicit format-word normalization agree with the published answer for the complete groups
cases.helper_observation: bits --width 5 correctly returns invalid_input/2 after explicit symbol mapping because of the partial trailing group
cases.recommendation: Keep the strict check. State group width, bit significance and letter/figure shifts; any dropped suffix is an explicit unresolved limitation
limitations: Three trailing symbols remain unexplained; no whole-input decoding-complete claim
Participant solver silently truncates and ignores figure mode; do not copy these shortcuts

cases.guide_route: Malware Analysis and Reverse Engineering / static unpacking
cases.evidence: writeup-informed static transform reproduced; key not independently derived
observations: 209408-byte PE holds an encrypted blob at RVA 0xf370, file offset 57200, length 104960
Published AES-128-ECB parameters produce a valid AMD64 DLL with 6 sections and one answer-shaped string
cases.helper_observation: File preview and XOR helper do not perform PE RVA translation or AES unpacking
cases.recommendation: Use approved disassembler/Python route, translate RVA to file offset, verify complete ciphertext bounds and decrypted PE headers before interpreting output
limitations: Published key/RVA used, not independently recovered from stub
Original packer, DLL and downloaded solver were never executed
No dynamic malware analysis or platform acceptance tested

pwn_source_only.evidence: static binary inspection; no exploitation claim
observations: main passes the fgets-populated buffer as printf format at 0x9aa, then calls gets at 0x9ca
Stack protector and a separate marker check appear before return
Participant solver claims positional leaks and libc ROP using pinned libc; not reproduced
pwn_source_only.recommended_mapping: Miscellaneous / native exploitation, with Reverse Engineering for static analysis
limitations: No ABI-specific offset or ROP chain validated
2022 year attribution from participant repository; official challenge-level provenance not independently established

additional_unreproduced.unlock2019: Downloaded ZIP and writeup; TLS decryption with bundled RSA key is a writeup claim here, not locally reproduced.
additional_unreproduced.n2_2025: TShark independently identified 753 packets: 5 SIP and 748 RTP. Audio extraction/Morse decoding remains writeup claim.
additional_unreproduced.web2019: Broken router and broken user management writeups inspected; server code absent. Firmware example ZIP is not a complete replayable web service.

Naive raw NTLM signature count saw duplicate type 2; corrected by comparing challenge and stream-aware TShark dissection.
Naive Scapy payload bytes included Ethernet padding in five FTP packets; corrected using IPv4 total length and header sizes.
